items.after:
- New `src/config.js` exporting one `CONFIG` object with the gameplay
  tunables: `zombieCount`, `humanCount`, all four move intervals,
  `infectionDelay`, `tigerFleeRange`, `tigerPanicRange`, `bunnyChaseRange`,
  `petDuration`. Structural/rendering constants (grid dims, cell size, radii,
  colors, key maps) stay module-level — they are not tuning values.
- `actors.js` reads `CONFIG.zombieCount`/`humanCount` and drops its
  `ZOMBIE_COUNT`/`HUMAN_COUNT` exports (nothing else imports them).
- `main.js` reads every tuning value from `CONFIG`.
- Track `saved` (humans that reached the Exit); when `humans` is empty, end
  the game: set a `gameOver` flag, stop further movement, and show an overlay
  with the outcome and score.

Win/lose rule (the one design fork here):

- **[chosen]** win if `saved > humanCount / 2` — a majority saved; else lose.
- alt: win only if every human is saved (strict, near-impossible against 4 zombies).
- alt: no binary verdict — show the score only.

- Overlay shows "You win/lose — saved X of N humans" plus "Press R to
  restart"; `onKeyDown("r")` reloads the page for a fresh map, guarded by
  `gameOver`.
items.before:
The game has no ending. Humans leave `humans` when they exit (item 7) or
convert to zombies (item 6), but nothing detects the empty board, no score is
tracked, and there is no win/lose display or restart. Gameplay tunables are
scattered: `actors.js` hardcodes `ZOMBIE_COUNT`/`HUMAN_COUNT`, and `main.js`
holds move intervals, infection delay, and flee/panic/chase ranges as
module-level `const`s — the plan's "centralized tuning" assumption calls for
one config object.
